paragraphs: Rav Matnah—Matna (II). He was a student of Rav Chisda. In [Kiddushin 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32a.15): Rav Yitzchak bar Shila transmits a ruling from Rav Matnah in Rav Chisda’s name. He was a colleague of Abaye: in [Ketubot 35b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.35b.6), Rav Matna said to Abaye, “According to Resh Lakish, who says,” etc.; and in [Shabbat 2b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.2b.15-16) he said to Abaye, “Are they eight? They are twelve!” Abaye replied,

“According to your reasoning, they are sixteen.” He said, “This is no difficulty.” In [Gittin 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.59b.14), Rav Matnah said, “What you said (Abaye), in the synagogue,” etc. Rav Ashi received teaching from this Rav Matnah toward the latter’s old age. In [Zevachim 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.29a.5-7), Rav Ashi said, “I stated the teaching before Rav Matnah,” who replied, “If from there,” etc. Seder HaDorot writes that this was the earlier Rav Ashi,

but overlooked that the statement concerns Rava and Rav Pappa, and consequently confused the first and second Rav Matna. Possibly the first was called Rav Matnah and the second Rav Matna, and inattentive copyists sometimes transferred one spelling to the other. Hyman considers it certain, however, that there were two. In [Sanhedrin 84b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.84b.13) he disagrees with Rav

notes.text: Matnah/Matna are different spellings. Hyman tentatively associates them with two sages but considers the existence of two figures certain.

The inspected Shabbat count discussion runs from 2b into 3a, preserving 8/12/16, and reads Matnah מתנה at that locus where Hyman supplies Matna מתנא. Zevachim 29a directly has Papa addressing Rava before Ashi’s report to Matnah, the context cited in Hyman’s argument. Hyman considers the existence of two figures certain while his proposed association of spellings with them is tentative. The direct passages do not independently prove that identity division or the proposed copyist history.

Kiddushin has Rav Yitzchak bar Shila transmit through Rav Matnah in Rav Chisda’s name. Shabbat reads Matnah (מתנה) and continues the count on 3a. Zevachim has Papa address Rava before Ashi reports his exchange with Matnah. Hyman treats the existence of two sages as certain and the spelling distinction as a possibility. See also [Shabbat 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.3a.1-4).
